$comment: Generated by scripts/preprocess-cmb.sh (scripts/cmb). Do not edit by hand.

uv.u: u = (0.5 - l/360) mod 1, l in degrees; inverse l = (180 - 360u) mod 360. u = 0 and u = 1 are both l = 180.
uv.v: v = 0.5 + b/180: v = 0 is the south galactic pole (b = -90), v = 1 the north galactic pole (b = +90).
uv.texelCentres: u = (i + 0.5)/W, v = (k + 0.5)/H, where k counts stored rows from the first one.
uv.rowOrder: bottom-up: the first stored row of every mip level is the southernmost (b near -90). The KTX2 files carry KTXorientation 'ru' to say so.
uv.loader: three's KTX2Loader keeps flipY = false (compressed textures cannot be flipped), so uv.y = 0 samples the first stored row, i.e. the south galactic pole. Use the texture as loaded; do not flip.
uv.wrap: wrapS = RepeatWrapping (longitude wraps at u = 0/1); wrapT = ClampToEdgeWrapping.

sphere.directionToUv: For a unit direction in galactic Cartesian coordinates (x toward l = 0, b = 0; y toward l = 90, b = 0; z toward the north galactic pole): l = atan2(y, x) in degrees, b = asin(z), then u and v as above.
sphere.threeSphereGeometryTrue: three's SphereGeometry has uv.y = 1 at +y and uv.x running right-handed about +y from -x. Sampling the texture at (1 - uv.x, uv.y) maps the galactic frame by a proper rotation: Galactic centre (l = 0, b = 0) on +x, l = 90 on -z, north galactic pole on +y. Every point is in its true direction: from the centre (BackSide) it looks like the sky; from outside it is that sphere seen from beyond, the mirror image of the published map.
sphere.threeSphereGeometryAsPublished: Sampling at (uv.x, uv.y) unchanged shows, from outside, the map as published (l increasing to the left); this is a reflection of the true geometry.
sphere.facingCamera: In both cases rotation.y = -PI/2 turns the Galactic centre toward a camera on +z.

rangeSource: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A1 (Planck 2018 results. I), figure 'Planck CMB sky', top panel (2018 SMICA temperature map): colour bar -300 to 300 uK. Checked in the arXiv:1807.06205 source, file moll_temp_v2.jpg.
outOfRange: clamped to the end colours (0.41% of texels; texel values span -512 to 526 uK)

colormap.name: planck
colormap.interpolation: linear between stops in sRGB-encoded values (the CSS linear-gradient default); position 0 = -300 uK, 1 = +300 uK

source.note: From the Planck collaboration's public figure style-guide examples (github.com/zonca/paperplots, A. Zonca, 2013). No primary ESA/PLA download of the table was found. Verified against the colour bar of the Planck 2018 results I SMICA figure: mean absolute difference about 2.5/255 per channel (JPEG noise).

smoothing.kernel: Gaussian in harmonic space: healpy.smoothing, ring weights, iter = 3, lmax = 3 NSIDE - 1

resampling: bilinear HEALPix interpolation (healpy.get_interp_val) at every texel centre
mipmaps: 13 levels, 4096x2048 down to 1x1, made offline with a 2x2 box filter in linear light; cmb-2048 holds levels 1 to the end of the same chain

temperature.format: R8_UNORM, linear, zstd level 19 supercompression (lossless), box-filtered mip chain
temperature.rows: bottom-up (v = 0 is the south galactic pole)
temperature.encoding: value = (T - (-300)) / 600 in uK, clamped to 0..1, stored as round(255 * value)
temperature.tool: ktx create --format R8_UNORM --assign-tf linear --assign-texcoord-origin bottom-left --generate-mipmap --mipmap-filter box --zstd 19 (KTX-Software, unpacked by fetch-ktx.sh)

convention.description: grid sampled at the documented (u,v) of 20000 random (l,b) vs direct HEALPix lookup; the residual is texel-scale interpolation. Controls: same with l mirrored (as if l increased to the right) and with b flipped.

coldSpotMeanUk.description: area-weighted mean within 5 deg; controls are the mirrored positions

galacticPlaneStdUk.description: std of the grid by |b| band; a foreground stripe would inflate the first

planck2018Figure.figure: Planck 2018 results I, SMICA temperature map (arXiv:1807.06205 moll_temp_v2.jpg)
